sections.html: One should keep these extremely rare gobies in an unheated tank with sandy bottom, pebbles and a good current.
In this goby the females are more colorful than the males. Females have a broad orange saddle on the back. The males can be recognized by the enormous mouth cleft.

The genus Schismatogobius currently contains 10 described species. All are small, only 3-5 cm long, pure freshwater inhabitants. As no species is of commercial value and the tiny fish bury themselves extremely fast in the sand when disturbed, the whole genus is so far only very unsatisfactorily researched. Two species have been reported from Taiwan: Schismatogobius ampluvinculus, which was described scientifically only in 1995, and S. roxasi. Both species are very similar to each other, but only S. ampluvinculus exhibits, in some moods, the strange, very contrasting black-and-white banding.
